seo.title: Homeless help in Phoenix - No Home Help
seo.description: Verified help for people experiencing homelessness or a housing crisis in Phoenix: shelter, heat safety, meals, health care, benefits, work, identification, and legal support.

content.text: Immediate danger, fire, overdose, or medical emergency:

notice.text: Beds, meals, funding, transport, hours, and eligibility can change.

Call or check the linked provider page before traveling when possible. No listing guarantees a bed, meal, treatment, payment, document, benefit, ride, or job. Call 911 for immediate danger or a life-threatening medical emergency.

content.text: Phoenix uses separate access routes for single adults, families, young people, veterans, and survivors of domestic violence. Tell staff your age, household members, exact location, health or mobility needs, pregnancy, veteran status, service animal or pet, and whether you are safe tonight.
Best first step for a single adult:

go to the Brian Garcia Welcome Center, 206 S. 12th Avenue, or call first. The facility is open 24 hours; Keys to Change publishes assessment and service-plan hours of 7:00 a.m.–11:00 p.m. CASS beds are assigned in person, first come and first served; they cannot be reserved by phone or email.
provides practical signposting, not emergency response, legal advice, medical advice, or a guarantee of service.

categories.title: 1. Urgent help, outreach, and extreme heat

content.text: Call for immediate violence, fire, heat stroke, overdose, unconsciousness, severe breathing trouble, heavy bleeding, serious injury, or another life-threatening emergency. Give the exact location or nearest landmark and describe the danger first.
City of Phoenix — Office of Homeless Solutions

Request outreach for someone living outside or report an encampment. Give an exact location and describe urgent health or safety needs. Outreach cannot force a person to accept services and does not guarantee a shelter bed. Homelessness itself is not a crime; call 911 for immediate danger.
City of Phoenix — coordinated homeless response

items.name: Heat safety and current seasonal status

content.text: Phoenix's dedicated 2026 heat-relief sites closed for the season on October 1, 2026. Do not travel to the former 24-hour site at 20 W. Jackson Street expecting it to be open. Phoenix Public Library locations continue to offer air-conditioned space during normal hours. Call 211 for a current open location.
The regional Heat Relief Network normally operates May 1–September 30. Check the live network before relying on any seasonal site or extended hours.
City of Phoenix — 2026 heat-site closure notice

Move to shade or air conditioning, loosen clothing, cool the skin, and sip water if the person is awake and able to swallow. Confusion, fainting, seizures, very hot skin, or inability to drink can mean heat stroke: call 911 and cool the person while help is coming.
Free, confidential crisis support for suicidal thoughts, emotional distress, mental-health crisis, or urgent substance-use concerns. Call 911 when there is immediate physical danger.

Ask for an open shelter access point, meal, cooling location, health service, benefit office, or transport option. Give your ZIP code or nearest cross streets and confirm details directly with the provider.

items.name: Brian Garcia Welcome Center — single adults

content.text: The facility is open 24 hours. Keys to Change publishes assessment and service-plan hours of 7:00 a.m.–11:00 p.m. Staff can assess needs and discuss CASS, Respiro, other shelter, benefits, health care, and housing navigation. A visit does not guarantee placement.

items.name: Central Arizona Shelter Services — adults age 18+

content.text: Brian Garcia Welcome Center, 206 S. 12th Avenue

Single-adult beds are assigned through in-person intake, first come and first served. CASS does not reserve beds by phone or email. Bring photo ID, medications, and useful documents if you have them, but ask for document-replacement help if you do not. People age 55+ can ask about The Haven, which is referral based.

items.name: Family Housing Hub — families with a child under 18

content.text: This is the regional entry route for families with dependent children. A waiting list may be used. Explain the household size, children's ages, pregnancy, immediate safety, disability or medical needs, and whether you have transport. Do not go to CASS expecting family intake.

items.name: Halle Women's Center — single women without children

content.text: 3424 E. Van Buren Street, Phoenix, AZ 85008
Call about the current waitlist, intake, eligibility, and what to do tonight if no space is available. A call does not reserve a bed.

Emergency shelter and a weekday drop-in center. The provider publishes drop-in hours Monday–Friday, 7:00 a.m.–4:00 p.m., with showers, laundry, food, rest space, and case management. Call about shelter intake and current capacity.
Ask for immediate safety planning and youth shelter help. If a young person is in immediate danger, call 911.

Street outreach, basic supplies, recovery programs, and residential program screening. The men's Transforming Lives Center is at 1801 S. 35th Avenue; the women's and children's Changing Lives Center is at 338 N. 15th Avenue. These are structured Christian recovery programs, not guaranteed walk-in emergency beds. Call first about requirements.

Safe Outdoor Space, the Navigation Center, and Respiro generally use referrals and are not reliable public walk-in options. Ask the Welcome Center, PHX C.A.R.E.S., or an outreach worker whether a referral is appropriate and currently available.
Saturday–Thursday, 5:00–6:00 p.m.; line begins at 4:00 p.m.
Community dinner and basic services. André House is Catholic and says it welcomes every person. Check the current weekly calendar before a long trip.

items.name: St. Vincent de Paul — Phoenix Dining Room

content.text: breakfast Monday–Friday, 7:00–8:00 a.m.; lunch daily, 11:00 a.m.–12:45 p.m.; dinner Friday, 4:00–5:00 p.m.
Walk-in adult dining room. Seasonal afternoon heat relief runs June 1–September 30 and is closed now. St. Vincent de Paul is Catholic; its meal page does not state that worship is required.
St. Vincent de Paul — Phoenix Dining Room

items.name: St. Vincent de Paul — Family Evening Meal

content.text: For families accompanied by a child under 18. Call about current access before traveling.
St. Vincent de Paul — meals and food boxes
No appointment is listed. Bring ID if you have it. Ask what alternatives are accepted if you have no ID and whether any clothing fee applies to your household.

items.name: St. Mary's Food Bank — Phoenix Food Center

content.text: Call or check the current distribution calendar and ask about household, ZIP code, ID, and frequency rules before traveling.
. Give your ZIP code or nearest cross streets, household size, transport limits, and dietary or mobility needs. Confirm the schedule with the provider.

categories.title: 4. Showers, laundry, clothing, mail, and storage

items.name: Lodestar Day Resource Center — Key Campus

content.text: Day room, navigation, benefit partners, showers, limited clothing, storage, mail, document help, and other scheduled services. Individual services have different hours and some are first come, first served. Call or ask the Welcome Center for the current schedule.
Key Campus — service map and schedule

Ask the mailroom before using this address. Confirm that you are registered, the exact name format, accepted items, collection hours, ID rules, and how long mail is held. Do not send important documents until staff confirms the procedure.

items.name: André House — showers, laundry, clothing, and hygiene

content.text: showers Monday–Thursday, 12:30–3:00 p.m.; laundry Monday–Wednesday, 8:30 a.m.–12:00 p.m., with limited slots and an earlier line; clothing Tuesday and Thursday, 12:30–3:00 p.m., and Saturday, 1:00–3:00 p.m.; hygiene supplies on selected afternoons. Arrive early and check for closures.

items.name: Justa Center — adults age 55 and older

content.text: Showers, laundry, hygiene items, meals, lockers, mail, document storage, computers, benefits help, health services, and housing navigation for people age 55+. Intake is published daily from 7:00–9:00 a.m.; walk-in space is limited. Normal hours are 7:00 a.m.–2:30 p.m.; extended summer hours end after October.

Shelter guests receive meals, hygiene, showers, restrooms, case management, and secure mail. Some services may have limited access for people not staying there; call first rather than assuming walk-in access.

categories.title: 5. Health, dental, mental health, and substance-use help

items.name: Circle the City — Downtown Family Health Center

content.text: Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m.–8:00 p.m.; weekends, 8:00 a.m.–5:00 p.m.; closed 12:00–1:00 p.m.

Primary and preventive care for people experiencing homelessness, including chronic-disease care, immunizations, behavioral-health and substance-use consultation, case management, and care coordination. Walk-ins and appointments are supported; call about current access.

items.name: Circle the City — Parsons Family Health Center

content.text: Primary, preventive, behavioral-health, substance-use, case-management, and pediatric care. Call about walk-ins, appointments, cost, insurance, and documents.
Circle the City — locations and hours

items.name: Mobile medical care and medical respite

content.text: Medical respite is short-term clinical recovery for eligible people referred after illness, injury, or hospital care. It is not a public walk-in shelter and does not guarantee acceptance.

Dental care for adults experiencing homelessness, veterans, and low-income older adults. Treatment fees apply; any assistance is assessed separately. Confirm intake, appointment availability, fees, and eligibility before traveling.

items.name: Solari Warm Line — peer support before a crisis

content.text: Free, confidential peer support for adults age 18+ dealing with loneliness, mental-health concerns, substance use, or recovery. Use 988 for a crisis and 911 for immediate danger.

Sonoran Prevention Works publishes current outreach sites and ways to obtain naloxone. Schedules change, so contact the listed provider before traveling. Pharmacies may also dispense naloxone under Arizona's standing order; call first about stock and cost.
If someone may be overdosing, call 911, give naloxone if available, and stay with the person. More than one dose may be needed.

categories.title: 6. Benefits, housing, rent, and utility help

items.name: Health-e-Arizona Plus — AHCCCS, SNAP, and cash assistance

content.text: Apply for Arizona Medicaid health coverage, Nutrition Assistance, and Cash Assistance; renew benefits; report changes; and ask for application help. The online portal has had service interruptions in 2026, so use the phone line or ask a community-assistor organization if the site is unavailable.

items.name: Phoenix Family Services Centers — crisis assistance

content.text: Ask about current emergency rent, mortgage, or utility assistance, case management, and eligibility. Funding and appointment availability change and are not guaranteed.

Single adults can begin at the Welcome Center; families should use the Family Housing Hub; young adults ages 18–24 should use a youth access point; veterans should use the VA Community Resource and Referral Center. Assessment does not guarantee a housing voucher, apartment, or shelter bed.

items.name: Preventing eviction — act before the court date

content.text: Call the Phoenix crisis-assistance line and Community Legal Services as soon as you receive a notice. Keep the notice, lease, payment records, messages, identification, and proof of income. Do not ignore court papers. Assistance and representation depend on eligibility, deadlines, and capacity.
City of Phoenix — service and eviction-help brochure

Call for routes, first and last trips, fares, accessibility, and service changes. Exact cash is needed on buses and drivers do not give change. Do not board without confirming the current fare or a valid pass.
Valley Metro — hours and customer service

Reduced fare is available on local bus and light rail for youth ages 6–18, adults age 65+, Medicare cardholders, and eligible people with disabilities. Proof and an application are required; approval is not immediate.
Valley Metro Mobility Center, 4600 E. Washington Street, Suite 101.

items.name: Phoenix Public Library — computers, Wi-Fi, and cooling

content.text: Libraries provide air-conditioned space during normal hours, public Wi-Fi, and computer access. Ask about guest computer access, card requirements, printing, scanning, charging, and current branch hours. Burton Barr has construction and service changes during 2025–26, so call before traveling.
Phoenix Public Library — computers and internet

The campus service map lists Elaine transportation on a schedule. It is not an on-demand or guaranteed ride. Ask the Welcome Center or Lodestar Day Resource Center about current destinations, eligibility, pickup times, and capacity.

Job-search help, computers, career planning, training referrals, résumé assistance, adult education, reentry, youth, and vocational-rehabilitation partner services. Call for current hours, orientation, required documents, and the best center for your needs. Services do not guarantee employment.

Employment support for people facing barriers, including job search, résumé and interview help, work clothing or tools when available, and employment planning. Call about orientation, eligibility, current hours, and documents. Assistance does not guarantee a job or financial help.
Ask about job-search help, résumés, applications, computers, interview preparation, and current appointment availability.
Use public computers and Wi-Fi for applications and email. Ask staff about guest access, printing, scanning, résumé resources, and current workforce programs.
Phoenix Public Library — computers and internet

items.name: Homeless ID Project — Arizona ID and birth certificates

content.text: 1125 W. Jackson Street, inside the Lodestar Day Resource Center
Monday–Friday, 8:00 a.m.–1:00 p.m.; closed the second Wednesday and third Monday of each month; first come, first served.
Help obtaining Arizona identification and birth certificates. Arrive early and ask what proof is needed, which states are covered, whether fees apply, and how documents will be delivered.

A standard Arizona ID generally costs $12 and requires proof of identity, a Social Security number, and two proofs of Arizona residency. People age 65+, SSI recipients, and eligible homeless veterans may qualify for a no-fee card. A standard ID is not a federal REAL ID.
Ask Homeless ID Project or a caseworker to identify acceptable documents and residency evidence before visiting MVD.

items.name: Maricopa County Vital Records — Arizona birth certificate

content.text: Monday, Tuesday, Thursday, and Friday, 8:00 a.m.–4:30 p.m.; Wednesday, 9:00 a.m.–4:30 p.m.
A certified Arizona birth certificate is listed at $20. Eligibility, application, and identity requirements apply. Use Homeless ID Project first if you lack the required ID or fee.
. Ask about replacing a Social Security card, updating a record, SSI or SSDI, and the nearest office. Do not pay an unofficial website for a replacement card.
Social Security Administration — replace a card

items.name: Community Legal Services — civil legal aid

content.text: Legal aid may cover eviction, housing, benefits, consumer, family, farmworker, and other civil matters. Income and case eligibility apply. The central office currently limits walk-ins because of building repairs, so apply by phone or online unless the provider confirms otherwise.

items.name: City of Phoenix eviction legal services

content.text: Ask about current eviction legal assistance and document drop-off through Phoenix Family Services Centers. Keep every notice and court paper and call immediately; deadlines can be very short. Help depends on eligibility and capacity.
City of Phoenix — services and eviction help

Affordable immigration consultations and representation for family petitions, DACA, VAWA, U and T visas, green-card renewals, and citizenship. Call about fees, appointments, language access, and documents. Services and outcomes are not guaranteed.

The campus map lists Homeless Court on selected Tuesdays and Thursdays. Call first to confirm the schedule, eligible cases, referral requirements, documents, and whether you must already be working with a case manager.

categories.title: 11. Women, domestic violence, trafficking, and LGBTQ+ support

content.text: Confidential safety planning and screening for domestic-violence shelter. Call from a safe phone if possible. Shelter addresses may be confidential and space is not guaranteed. Call 911 for immediate danger.

items.name: Arizona Coalition to End Sexual and Domestic Violence

content.text: Information, safety planning, referrals, and legal advocacy for survivors. It is not a shelter-placement guarantee.
Use a safe device if someone monitors your phone. Ask for a safe plan, emergency referral, and language assistance. Call 911 if you are in immediate danger.

items.name: one·n·ten — LGBTQ+ youth and young adults

content.text: 1101 N. Central Avenue, Suite 104, Phoenix, AZ 85004

Affirming programs, basic resources, community support, and housing assistance for LGBTQ+ youth and young adults. Call about age limits, drop-in times, current housing navigation, and what is available today. This is not a guaranteed emergency shelter bed.

categories.title: 12. Families, youth, older adults, and disability needs

content.text: Ask about shelter assessment, the waitlist, documents, transport, school continuity, food, diapers, medical needs, and what to do tonight. Keep the phone available for callbacks if possible.

Youth services may help with shelter, showers, laundry, meals, school or employment, documents, health care, and housing navigation. Explain immediate safety, age, pregnancy, trafficking risk, LGBTQ+ safety concerns, and whether an adult controls your documents or phone.

Justa Center provides day services and housing navigation for people age 55+. The Senior Help Line can screen for older-adult services, caregiver help, benefits, and the DOVES domestic-violence program. Ask the Welcome Center about The Haven shelter referral.

Tell every access point about wheelchair or walker use, oxygen, medication refrigeration, communication needs, service animals, inability to stand in line, or need for an accessible bed or restroom. Ask for a reasonable accommodation and accessible transport.
For Valley Metro reduced fare and paratransit information, call
. For benefit screening and long-term-care questions, call

items.name: VA Community Resource and Referral Center

content.text: 1500 E. Thomas Road, Suite 106, rear of building, Phoenix, AZ 85014

Coordinated access for veterans experiencing homelessness, including assessment, health and benefit connections, outreach, housing programs, and referrals. Bring military or identity documents if available, but call even if they are missing. Placement and financial help are not guaranteed.

items.name: National Call Center for Homeless Veterans

content.text: For veterans who are homeless or at risk and people calling on their behalf. Ask about local VA outreach, shelter, housing, medical care, and benefits.
U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs — homeless veteran call center

Arizona MVD may waive the fee for an eligible homeless veteran. MVD verifies veteran status and may require a recent homelessness statement from VA or a verified provider. Ask the VA center or Homeless ID Project to prepare the correct paperwork first.

items.name: Ask before traveling with an animal

content.text: Tell the shelter whether the animal is a trained service animal, emotional-support animal, or pet; species and size; vaccination status; crate or leash; and whether temporary foster care would be acceptable. Policies and space differ. Do not abandon an animal because one program says no.
. The office is not open to the public and is not an animal shelter.
Request assistance for pet food, veterinary barriers, housing problems, domestic-violence safety, or another crisis that could separate you from a pet. Help depends on eligibility and capacity.
The Arizona Pet Project lists Helping Hands for Homeless Hounds at
and Lost Our Home Pet Rescue at
. Call first: an application, appointment, geographic limit, or waitlist may apply.
Arizona Pet Project — pet housing resources

The free PHX Sky Train connects Terminals 3 and 4 with the Valley Metro Rail station at 44th Street and Washington Street. Valley Metro fare is required for the light-rail portion. Check route and operating information before relying on a late-night connection.

An airport is not a shelter. Remaining in terminals without a travel purpose may lead to contact with airport staff or police. If you need shelter, use 211 or the Welcome Center before going to the airport.
Phoenix Sky Harbor — PHX Sky Train

Do not assume a shelter, outreach team, church, or city office will buy a ticket. If safe reunification is possible, ask a caseworker whether a verified transportation program exists and what proof is needed. Never hand identity documents or money to an unofficial broker.

items.text: Call 911 for immediate danger, serious illness, heat stroke, or overdose. Use 988 for a mental-health or substance-use crisis.
Single adults: Welcome Center. Families: 211 or Family Housing Hub. Ages 12–17: Safe Place. Ages 18–24: HomeBase. Veterans: VA center. Domestic violence: the confidential screening line.
Dedicated 2026 heat sites are closed for the season, but dangerous heat can occur outside it. Use a library during normal hours or call 211 for an open indoor location.
Check André House, St. Vincent de Paul, NourishPHX, Key Campus, or Justa Center according to your age and today's schedule.
Keep papers dry, photograph them if safe, write down medication names, and ask about secure mail or storage. Do not use a mailing address without permission.
Start benefits and ID work early.
Use Health-e-Arizona Plus, Homeless ID Project, and a caseworker. Ask what alternate proof is accepted.

“Is intake open now?”, “Can I enter today?”, “What ID is required?”, “Is there a fee?”, “Can you accommodate my disability, service animal, pet, medication, partner, or children?”, and “What should I do if there is no space?”
Write down at least two options, the name of the person you spoke with, and the time to call back. Availability can change before you arrive.

content.text: report a closed service, changed phone number, or missing local resource through the project repository. Do not publish a survivor's location, private medical information, or another person's personal details.
